issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator commits legal misconduct by receiving and considering evidence from one party in the absence of the other party, without giving the absent party an opportunity to answer it, and the misconduct vitiates the award regardless of proof of prejudice.
material_facts: The parties referred their pending civil dispute to a sole arbitrator and agreed to abide by the award.
The arbitrator separately examined each side and obtained a statement from one party containing factual assertions beyond that party’s pleadings.
The arbitrator considered that statement and a settlement document when making the award.
The other party received no notice of the separate examination and had no opportunity to cross-examine, respond to the evidence, or present evidence to meet it.
issues.conclusion: The arbitrator was guilty of legal misconduct, which was sufficient to vitiate the award even without proof that the misconduct caused prejudice.
issues.legal_principle: The principles of natural justice require both sides to be heard in each other’s presence and prohibit one side from using material to influence the decision-maker that the other side does not know of and cannot meet. This applies to arbitration as well as court proceedings. The Court relied on Harvey v. Shelton (1844) 7 Beav. 455, Ganesh Narayan Singh v. Malida Koer (1911) 13 Cal. L.J. 399, Walker v. Frobisher (1801) 6 Ves. 70, and Haigh v. Haigh (1861) 31 L.J. Ch. 420; the arbitration was referred under section 21 of the Indian Arbitration Act.

rule.if: arbitration_proceeding and award_made and arbitrator_received_one_sided_evidence and other_party_lacked_opportunity_to_answer

predicates.arbitration_proceeding: The dispute was referred to an arbitrator for decision.
predicates.award_made: The arbitrator issued an award resolving the referred dispute.
predicates.arbitrator_received_one_sided_evidence: The arbitrator received evidence from one party outside the presence of the other party.
predicates.other_party_lacked_opportunity_to_answer: The absent party had no opportunity to know of and respond to the evidence before the decision was made.

issues.definition: When an arbitrator issues an award after receiving one-sided evidence that the other party had no opportunity to answer, the award is vitiated.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot raise an unpleaded waiver contention for the first time at the appellate stage.
material_facts: The party opposing the challenge to the award had not pleaded that the challenger waived the right to contest the award.
That party nevertheless argued waiver before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The waiver contention was not competent to be raised at that stage because waiver had not been pleaded.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to entertain the waiver contention because it had not been pleaded below and was raised at the appellate stage; no provision or earlier case was cited for this ruling.

predicates.appellate_proceeding: A party is advancing a contention in an appellate proceeding.
predicates.waiver_not_pleaded_below: The party relying on waiver did not plead it in the proceedings below.
predicates.waiver_raised_at_appellate_stage: The party first advances the waiver contention at the appellate stage.

issues.definition: In an appellate proceeding, an appellate court rejects a waiver contention when it was not pleaded below and is raised only at the appellate stage.
